transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jasper (Redwood SE), Renee (Redwood CSM), Alex (SunPeak Inf), Priya (SunPeak Sec), Tom (Platform), Samir (Net)
Links mentioned: https://redwood.com/docs/private-kms-integration.pdf, https://redwood.com/decks/private-deployments.pdf, spreadsheet: https://redwood.com/benchmarks/sunpeak-run1.xlsx

Summary:
Quick intake focused on private onramp: how Redwood Private can be deployed into SunPeak VPCs, KMS/HSM control, peering vs privatelink, and region gating for EU data. SunPeak leaning heavy to owning keys (HSM) and wants strong audit trail + egress controls.

Topics covered:
- VPC peering vs PrivateLink/Private Endpoints
- KMS/HSM integration patterns and key custody
- Transit gateways / central egress vs spoke model
- Regional restrictions (EU-West, GovCloud mention)
- Latency expectations for Dedicated vs Private
- Next steps and benchmarks

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) ---
00:00 Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we know this is super busy week so we'll run through how Redwood Private can land in SunPeak, take notes, and then outline next steps.
00:14 Alex: Yeah thanks, happy to be here. Quick context, we're a data platform for energy forecasting, most traffic originates from EU and US east, we have strict PII residency for a subset of customers.
00:28 Priya: Role note, I'm the security lead, primary asks are KMS ownership, audit logs, and limited egress.
00:36 Jasper: Great, Jasper from Redwood infra, I'll walk through the network options and the KMS flow after Maya sets the scope.
00:45 Maya: Awesome. So, first question — are you expecting us to run in your VPC completely, or is the plan to use a private-managed plane with private endpoints? Which direction are you leaning?
00:56 Tom: Prefer keeping control of keys and traffic; so private in VPC ideally. We can consider a dedicated capacity model too, if it helps SLA.
01:06 Maya: Understood. Two patterns we see: 1) Full Private (Redwood Private deployed to customer VPCs/on-prem) where you retain networking and KMS, or 2) Private endpoints (Privatelink) to a Redwood-managed plane with customer-managed egress and optional KMS via external key. Both have tradeoffs.
01:22 Samir: Can you explain the peering approach? We use a Transit Gateway today.
01:26 Jasper: Sure. Peering is straightforward: we can peer Redwood service subnets with your VPCs, or you can set up VPC endpoints/privatelink. Peering requires route table changes and some IP planning; privatelink gives interface endpoints and is easier for cross-account isolation but can be region specific.
01:44 Alex: Is privatelink available in eu-west-1? We have most customers in Dublin.
01:48 Jasper: Yes, but there's nuance. Some regions have endpoint service quotas and different feature parity. For eu-west-1 we can do privatelink but for govcloud or some APAC regions might vary. We often recommend peering for multi-region transit gateway topologies.
02:05 Priya: KMS — we need to hold keys in our HSM. Will Redwood support external KMS/HSM where keys never leave our control?
02:11 Maya: Short answer yes. We support external KMS through customer-managed keys. For HSM we have an integration path where Redwood delegates envelope encryption and you keep the root keys. The initial setup needs a few steps: key policy, cross-account IAM roles or transient signing, and proofing in staging. We'll share the KMS guide.
02:32 Tom: How do audit logs look? We need token-level traceability and proof of access for regulators.
02:37 Jasper: We surface audit logs, and in Private you can ship all logs to your own CloudWatch/Stackdriver/ELK via our forwarder. There will be request IDs, model version, and token counts. Small caveat: some PII may be redacted depending on your retention; we'll align with your security team.
02:58 Priya: Who holds the TLS certs? If traffic is terminating at Redwood, we want mTLS or client certs.
03:05 Maya: For Private where we deploy into your VPC, traffic stays inside and you can control certs; we can support mTLS. For Privatelink to a Redwood plane, we use customer-managed certs on endpoints or mTLS as well.
03:20 Samir: Any differences in latency between peering and privatelink? We do low-latency inference for real-time dashboards.
03:25 Jasper: Peering (same AZ) tends to have lowest hop count; privatelink is a layer on top which can add microseconds. Dedicated hardware vs shared hosted also influences p99 latency. We'll capture baseline numbers in the mini-benchmark.
03:42 Alex: On the topic of Dedicated — what's the minimum commit and how does that affect placement?
03:46 Maya: Dedicated is usually a committed pool; placement can be in our region or colocated in your VPC depending on contract. For many customers we reserve capacity in the chosen region; if you need it inside your VPC that's a Private deployment with dedicated resources.
03:58 Priya: Data residency: we need assurance that certain datasets never leave EU. Can you guarantee model eval or logging won't cross regions?
04:05 Jasper: We can pin model serving and logging to a region. When keys are customer-controlled and endpoints are inside EU VPCs, nothing leaves unless you explicitly enable cross-region replication. We'll add configuration flags in the deployment template.
04:22 Tom: A practical ask: our IP space uses overlapping private CIDRs across orgs. How do you handle overlap?
04:27 Jasper: Overlap is common. Options: 1) use AWS PrivateLink (no routes needed), 2) assign a non-overlapping transit VPC, or 3) NAT and mapping. We typically prefer PrivateLink when overlap exists because it's cross-account and avoids route conflicts.
04:45 Alex: We also have strict outbound egress filtering — we can't allow unknown egress to the internet.
04:50 Maya: That's fine. We support egress via your transit GW or NAT: you can control egress IPs and we can whitelist. For hosted plane variant you'd need to allow Redwood egress IPs; for in-VPC you control it.
05:06 Priya: Any SOC2 docs or penetration test reports you can share?
05:11 Renee: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, and our security whitepaper. Link we'll send after.
05:18 Alex: About key rotation and KMS billing — we want to rotate monthly and have audit of every unwrap operation, is that feasible?
05:26 Jasper: Yes, you can rotate on your cadence; we call the KMS on envelope operations, and every decrypt/unseal can be logged in your KMS audit trail. Some performance cost small but manageable; Jasper will add KMS ops to perf doc.
05:40 Tom: Can you walk through a sample network diagram?
05:44 Jasper: Sure. [shares screen: diagram link referenced]. Topology: customer VPCs in EU and US, transit GW, Redwood Private nodes in a spoke VPC, peering or interface endpoints to the service. KMS in customer account with cross-account IAM to Redwood role for envelope operations.
06:08 Alex: For the transit model, do you require route propagation into our core RTs?
06:12 Jasper: We need specific route targets for the service CIDR; most customers add a route for the Redwood subnets to the TGW attachment. We'll provide a cutover checklist.
06:24 Samir: Security question: can we do VPC flow logs to our SIEM and mask tokens?
06:29 Jasper: Yes, flow logs can be shipped; token masking happens at application level — we can redact through our logging forwarder before it goes to your SIEM.
06:40 Priya: Are there any special quotas or limits that might block privatelink endpoints?
06:45 Maya: Region quotas for endpoint services can apply. We'll assess your account and help request quota increases if needed; often it's a trivial support ticket.
06:56 Alex: Let's talk about failover. If eu-west-1 has an outage, can we fail traffic to a secondary region without sending data outside EU?
07:04 Jasper: Cross-region failover typically moves traffic; to keep data in EU you'd need a secondary EU region like eu-central-1. We can set up canary routing and model replication to the second EU region. If you need strict residency, we replicate only to EU targets.
07:23 Tom: What about the tokenization/cache, the KV cache — is that stored in your control plane?
07:29 Jasper: KV cache for model state is per-node in the deployment; in Private it's inside your VPC and you control storage. For hosted plane we cache in our infra. Sometimes transcript notes show KV cash, but it's KV cache.
07:44 Alex: Pricing — if we keep KMS + private deployment, what does the pricing look like versus hosted?
07:49 Maya: Private inside customer VPC is priced as a platform fee plus resource usage; there is an ops premium for dedicated or on-prem. We will send a tailored estimate; initial ballpark is higher than hosted but gives control and compliance.
08:03 Priya: Any blockers around our HSM provider — we use a third party HSM in our account (Thales-like).
08:10 Jasper: We integrate with AWS CloudHSM and many partner HSMs via standard KMIP or BYOK flows. For unusual HSM vendors we'll validate, but envelope encryption model usually covers it.
08:22 Samir: Network testing — how do we validate latency and connectivity pre-prod?
08:26 Jasper: We stand up a test VPC, deploy a small Redwood node set, and run a perf harness (we'll send harness config). Jasper will run a controlled run and share the benchmark spreadsheet (link above).
08:38 Alex: Great. Who at Redwood will be our single point?
08:41 Maya: I'll own the commercial and timeline; Jasper takes technical lead; Renee is CSM for onboarding.
08:47 Maya: Quick real question — do you have an internal timeline for this?
08:50 Alex: We'd like a pilot in Q2, production by Q3. Main blocker is security signoff and network approvals.
08:57 Priya: We also need SAML/SSO integration with our IdP for auditing.
09:02 Jasper: We support SAML (SAML SSO) and can do SCIM for provisioning. Samel is sometimes mis-transcribed as SAMEL in older notes but yes SAML.
09:11 Tom: A minor thing — do you have any examples of route tables you need us to add?
09:15 Jasper: We'll provide a playbook with exact route entries, SG rules, and NACL recommendations.
09:22 Alex: On the Privatelink side, who pays for interface endpoint costs?
09:26 Maya: Usually the customer pays for the endpoint hours/data transfer. We'll call out TCO in the pricing doc.
09:33 Priya: Are logs signed for non-repudiation?
09:36 Jasper: We can timestamp and sign logs using your KMS and provide chain-of-trust artifacts. That is part of the more advanced compliance bundle.
09:50 Tom: If we go Private but later want to move to Redwood-managed dedicated, how difficult is migration?
09:54 Maya: We design for portability: model pins, versioning, and rolling cutovers. Migration is doable; some networking and KMS adjustments required.
10:05 Alex: Any limitations on model size or quantization options within Private?
10:09 Jasper: Mostly no — our runtime supports a variety of model sizes; certain quantization paths might require different kernels. We'll advise on recommended instance types for large models.
10:21 Priya: Last security note — we'd like to run a joint pen test against the deployment. Is that OK?
10:24 Renee: Yes, joint pen tests are supported; we'll coordinate scoping and acceptable testing windows.
10:30 Maya: Alright, let's recap next steps. Jasper will produce a short benchmark plan and KMS ops impact note, I'll send KMS/HSM integration guide and pricing estimate, and Alex will share network CIDRs and transit details.
10:48 Alex: Sounds good. Thank you.
10:52 Maya: Thanks everyone we'll follow up with the doc pack and schedule the diagram review.

End of call.

Notes on transcription artifacts: occasional mis-hearings (SAMEL vs SAML), numeric timings approximate, proper nouns sometimes truncated. The call included sharing of three artifacts: private-kms-integration.pdf, private-deployments.pdf, and bench run spreadsheet.
